test: Georgia DDS Knowledge Exam (Class C Instructional Permit / Class C License)
edition: Based on the Georgia Department of Driver Services Drivers Manual, online edition at dds.georgia.gov/drivers-manual (page last updated July 2026, accessed October 2026); the downloadable PDF on the DDS site is labelled 2023-2024

exam.rules: Georgia's knowledge exam is taken by first-time applicants for a Class C Instructional Permit (from age 15) and by new adult drivers without a valid license from another US state; applicants under 18 need a parent, guardian or responsible adult to sign and must show school enrollment. It is given on a walk-in basis at any DDS Customer Service Center (start at least 30 minutes before closing) and has two separately scored parts: a Road Signs test (20 questions, English only, at least 15 correct) and a Road Rules test (20 questions, some other languages available, at least 15 correct). You must pass both parts. The $10 permit/test fee is paid before every attempt and is not refunded. After a first failure you may retake the failed part the next day; after a second or later failure you must wait 7 days. Phones, notes or talking during the test count as a failure.

questions.q: What must you do when you come to this sign?
options: Come to a complete stop, then yield before going on
Slow down and go if no cars are coming
Stop only if other traffic is present
questions.explain: An eight-sided sign always means stop: make a full stop at the stop line (or before the crosswalk), then yield to pedestrians and close traffic.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Shapes of Signs: Octagon signs'

questions.q: What does this sign require you to do?
options: Speed up to merge ahead of traffic
Stop only when a train is coming
Always come to a full stop
Slow down, stop if necessary, and give the right-of-way
questions.explain: A triangle means yield: slow to a reasonable speed, stop if needed, and let traffic in or near the intersection go first.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Shapes of Signs: Triangle signs'

questions.q: If you see this sign facing you, what does it tell you?
options: Traffic on this road comes toward you; you must not go down it
The road is closed for construction ahead
You may enter only to turn right
questions.explain: The do-not-enter sign marks a one-way road with traffic coming toward you; you must not continue down that road.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Regulatory Signs: Do not enter sign'

questions.q: You see this sign while entering a ramp. What does it mean?
options: The ramp is closed to trucks
You are going against the allowed direction of a one-way road or ramp
You must merge to the left
questions.explain: The wrong-way sign warns that driving on that highway or ramp in your direction is not allowed. Stop and turn around safely.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Regulatory Signs: Wrong way sign'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: You may not turn around to go the opposite way here
The road curves back sharply ahead
U-turns are allowed only on green
questions.explain: A red circle and slash means 'no'; the U-shaped arrow shows that U-turns are prohibited at this location.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Regulatory Signs: No U turn sign'

questions.q: What does this sign tell you?
options: You may not make a right turn at this intersection
questions.explain: The black right arrow inside a red circle-slash means right turns are not permitted at this intersection.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Regulatory Signs: No right turn sign'

questions.q: At an intersection with this sign and a red light, what are you allowed to do?
options: Turn right without stopping if clear
Turn right after a full stop
Wait for the green light; turning on red is prohibited even after stopping
Turn left onto a one-way street after stopping
questions.explain: This sign cancels the usual right-turn-on-red rule: you may not turn while the light is red, even after a complete stop.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Regulatory Signs: No right turn on red after stop sign'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: Traffic may travel only in the direction of the arrow
Turn in the direction of the arrow now
Detour in the direction of the arrow
questions.explain: The one-way sign means traffic on that street may travel only in the direction the arrow points.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Regulatory Signs: One way sign'

questions.q: What does this sign tell you to do?
options: Keep to the right of the median or obstruction
Turn right at the next street
questions.explain: The keep-right sign requires traffic to pass on the right side of a median, island or obstruction.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Regulatory Signs: Keep right sign'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: 55 mph is a suggested speed for a curve
55 mph is the highest legal speed in this area under ideal conditions
questions.explain: A white speed limit sign is regulatory: 55 mph is the maximum permitted speed in that area. Drive slower when conditions require.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Regulatory Signs: Speed limit 55 sign'

questions.q: On a road with two or more lanes in your direction, what does this sign mean?
options: Slower vehicles should use the right lane(s)
Only trucks may use the right lane
Slow down because a curve is ahead
questions.explain: When two or more lanes go your way, slower traffic should travel in the right (outside) lanes, leaving the left lane for passing.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Regulatory Signs: Slower traffic keep right sign'

questions.q: This yellow pennant-shaped sign is posted on the left side of the road. What does it mark?
options: The end of a no-passing zone
The start of a no-passing zone; finish any pass before you reach it
questions.explain: The pennant sits on the left side of the highway at the beginning of a no-passing zone; any passing must be completed before reaching it.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Warning Signs: No passing zone sign'

questions.q: What does this round yellow sign warn you about?
options: A railroad crossing ahead; slow down, look, listen and be ready to stop
questions.explain: A round sign is the railroad advance warning sign, posted a few hundred feet before the tracks.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Shapes of Signs: Round signs'

questions.q: What should you do when you see this sign?
options: Always stop, even if no train is coming
Yield to any approaching train; slow down, look and listen before crossing
It is a guide sign with no action required
Speed up to clear the tracks quickly
questions.explain: The crossbuck is placed at all railroad crossings and means yield to trains. A full stop is required when red lights flash.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Guide Signs: Railroad crossing sign'

questions.q: What does this five-sided sign mean?
options: You are approaching a school zone or school crossing
questions.explain: Pentagon-shaped signs mark a school zone and/or school crossing, posted 150 to 700 feet ahead of the school grounds or crossing.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Shapes of Signs: Pentagon signs'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: A gentle curve to the right
A sharp turn to the right ahead
A side road on the right
questions.explain: The bent-arrow warning sign means the road makes a sharp turn to the right ahead. Slow down before the turn.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Warning Signs: Sharp right turn sign'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: The road you are on ends ahead; prepare to turn left or right
questions.explain: A T-shaped symbol means your road ends at a crossing road ahead. Slow down and prepare to yield or stop before turning.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Warning Signs: Road ends sign'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: Traffic is merging from the right; be ready to let it in
Your lane ends and you must merge right
questions.explain: The merge sign warns of traffic joining from the right. Adjust speed or position so it can merge safely.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Warning Signs: Merge sign'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: The number of lanes is reduced ahead
questions.explain: This sign shows a lane ending; the number of lanes is reduced ahead, so be ready to merge.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Warning Signs: Lanes reduced sign'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: The divided highway ends; traffic will travel in both directions without a median
A lane is added on the right
You are entering a one-way street
questions.explain: The divided-highway-ends sign means the median ends ahead. Be ready to change lanes or shift lane position.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Warning Signs: Divided highway ends sign'

questions.q: What does this warning sign mean?
options: Passing is allowed in both directions
You are leaving a one-way roadway; two-way traffic is ahead
questions.explain: The two-way-traffic sign warns that you are leaving a separated one-way highway and will soon share the road with oncoming traffic.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Warning Signs: Two way traffic sign'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: Traffic signals at the intersection ahead
questions.explain: The signal-ahead sign warns that there are traffic signals at the intersection ahead. Slow down.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Warning Signs: Signal ahead sign'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: A stop sign is ahead; begin slowing and be ready to stop
A school bus stop is ahead
A four-way stop is behind you
questions.explain: The stop-ahead sign warns of a stop sign ahead that may be hard to see. Slow down and prepare to stop.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Warning Signs: Stop ahead sign'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: The road is slippery when wet
questions.explain: The skid-mark symbol means the roadway is slippery when wet. The first half-hour of rain is the most hazardous.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Warning Signs: Slippery when wet sign'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: The bridge ahead is narrower than the road
questions.explain: The narrow-bridge sign means the bridge allows room for only two lanes of traffic. Approach with caution.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Warning Signs: Narrow bridge sign'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: Do not enter if your vehicle or load is taller than the height shown
questions.explain: This sign warns of a low underpass ahead. If your vehicle or its load is taller than the height shown, do not go under it.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Warning Signs: Low clearance sign'

questions.q: What should you expect when you see this sign?
options: People may be crossing the road ahead
questions.explain: Pedestrian crossing signs alert drivers in advance of areas where people may be crossing.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Warning Signs: Pedestrian and animal crossing signs'

questions.q: This orange sign tells you that you are approaching:
options: A road construction or maintenance area
questions.explain: Construction and maintenance warning signs are orange with black markings. Watch for orange: it means road work.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Construction and Maintenance Warning Signs'

questions.q: A vehicle displaying this orange triangle with a red border is:
options: A vehicle that is about to stop
A slow-moving vehicle traveling under 25 mph
questions.explain: This emblem marks a slow-moving vehicle, defined as one moving less than 25 mph. Such vehicles must display it.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Guide Signs: Caution sign'

questions.q: What does this yellow plaque below a warning sign tell you?
options: The distance to the next exit
The minimum speed on the highway
The maximum legal speed on all nearby roads
The suggested safe speed for the curve or hazard ahead
questions.explain: Advisory speed plaques show a recommended speed for a specific condition, usually lower than the posted limit.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Curves'

questions.q: What must you do when facing this signal?
options: Slow down and proceed with caution
Stop only if cars are coming
Make a complete stop before the crosswalk or intersection and wait for green
Speed up to clear the intersection
questions.explain: A steady red light means stop completely before the crosswalk or intersection and wait until it turns green (unless a legal turn on red is allowed).
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Traffic Signals and Signs: Red light'

questions.q: When facing this signal, you may go:
options: Only if it is safe, after yielding to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection
Immediately, because you have the right-of-way
questions.explain: A green light means proceed if safe; do not go 'just because' the light is green while the intersection is not clear.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Traffic Signals and Signs: Green light'

questions.q: What does this green arrow allow?
options: Turning left only after first coming to a complete stop
Turning left in the direction of the arrow after yielding to pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection
questions.explain: A green arrow allows movement only in the arrow's direction, after yielding to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Traffic Signals and Signs: Green left arrow'

questions.q: How should you treat this flashing signal?
options: The signal is off; go through
Like a stop sign: stop completely, then proceed when safe
Stop and wait for the light to turn green
Like a yield sign: slow down only
questions.explain: A flashing red light means stop completely as at a stop sign, then proceed after yielding to pedestrians and other vehicles.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Traffic Signals and Signs: Flashing red light'

questions.q: What does this flashing signal mean?
options: Slow down and proceed with caution
questions.explain: A flashing yellow light means slow down and use caution before proceeding through the intersection.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Traffic Signals and Signs: Flashing yellow light'

questions.q: What do these pavement markings in the center of a two-lane road mean?
options: Passing is allowed only on the left side
Passing is not allowed in either direction
The lanes carry traffic in the same direction
questions.explain: When both center yellow lines are solid, it is not safe to pass in either direction.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Pavement Markings: No Passing Lines'

questions.q: A single broken yellow center line on a two-lane road means:
options: The lane is reserved for left turns
Passing is allowed in either direction when it is safe
Traffic moves in the same direction
questions.explain: Broken yellow center lines are used where there are only two lanes and passing is safe in either direction.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Pavement Markings: Center Lines'

questions.q: You are driving the blue car on this two-lane road. Based on the center lines, may you pass the vehicle ahead?
options: No; any solid yellow line means no passing in either direction
Yes, when it is safe, because the broken line is on your side
Yes, but only on hills or curves
Only if the driver ahead signals you to pass
questions.explain: Each driver obeys the yellow line closest to their own lane. Here the broken line is on your side, so you may pass when it is safe; drivers on the other side, facing the solid line, may not.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Passing: How To Pass On A Two-Lane Road'

questions.q: A center lane marked like this may be used:
options: Only for making left turns, entering it no more than 300 feet before the turn
questions.explain: Georgia law prohibits using a center turn lane for any purpose other than a left turn, and you may enter it no more than 300 feet before the turn.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Pavement Markings: Turn Lanes'

questions.q: In Georgia, how many basic sign shapes are used to convey traffic control instructions?
questions.explain: The manual states that Georgia uses seven basic sign shapes so drivers can recognize signs from a distance.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Shapes of Signs'

questions.q: If a traffic signal at an intersection is completely dark (not working), you must:
options: Yield only to vehicles on your left
Treat it like a flashing yellow light
Proceed without stopping if you are on the larger road
Treat the intersection as an all-way stop
questions.explain: When a signal is not functioning at all, every driver must treat the intersection as if stop signs were posted in all directions.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Traffic Signals and Signs'

questions.q: A flashing yellow left-turn arrow means you may turn left:
options: After yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, since oncoming traffic has a green light
Only when the arrow turns steady
Without yielding, because you have a protected turn
questions.explain: A flashing yellow arrow allows a left turn after yielding; oncoming traffic still has a green light.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Traffic Signals and Signs: Flashing yellow arrow'

questions.q: At a Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon (PHB), the alternating flashing red lights mean drivers must:
options: Wait until the beacon goes dark even if the crosswalk is empty
Stop fully, then go once pedestrians have cleared the crosswalk
questions.explain: During alternating flashing red, drivers must stop and may proceed once pedestrians have cleared the crosswalk.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Pedestrian-Hybrid Beacons (PHB)'

questions.q: When a stop line is painted at an intersection, where must you stop?
options: Wherever you can see best, even past the line
questions.explain: When a stop line is painted, that is where you must stop completely, not at the sign or signal itself.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Pavement Markings: Stop Lines'

questions.q: Solid double white lines between lanes mean:
options: Lane changes across them are prohibited
You may cross them with care
questions.explain: Solid double white lines prohibit lane changes; dashed double white lines allow crossing to the adjacent lane.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Pavement Markings: No Passing Lines'

questions.q: Two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals) at the same time. Who must yield?
options: The driver on the right yields to the driver on the left
The driver going faster has the right-of-way
The driver on the left yields to the driver on the right
The larger vehicle has the right-of-way
questions.explain: At intersections without signs or signals, when two vehicles arrive together the vehicle on the left yields to the one on the right.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Laws Governing Right-of-Way'

questions.q: At a four-way stop, in what order should vehicles proceed?
options: First to arrive, first to proceed, after yielding to pedestrians
Vehicles on the busier street first
questions.explain: Where all approaches have stop signs, yield to pedestrians, then go in first-to-arrive, first-to-proceed order.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Laws Governing Right-of-Way'

questions.q: At a four-way stop, you and another driver arrive at about the same time. The other car is on your right. What should you do?
options: Go first because you are on the left
Both drivers should go at once
Go first if you are going straight
Yield to the car on your right
questions.explain: If two vehicles reach an all-way stop at about the same time, yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Laws Governing Right-of-Way'

questions.q: When turning left at an intersection or into a driveway, you must yield to:
options: All traffic coming from the opposite direction
No one if your signal is on
questions.explain: A left-turning driver must yield the right-of-way to all oncoming traffic, including bicycles, and to pedestrians crossing.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Laws Governing Right-of-Way'

questions.q: You are entering a road from a private driveway or alley. What must you do?
options: Yield only to vehicles on your left
Enter quickly to match traffic speed
Sound your horn and pull out
Stop and yield to all pedestrians and vehicles already on the road or sidewalk
questions.explain: When entering or crossing a highway from an alley, private road or driveway, stop and yield to all pedestrians and vehicles already there.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Laws Governing Right-of-Way'

questions.q: An emergency vehicle with lights and siren is approaching. What should you do?
options: Speed up to get out of its way
Slow down, move to the right edge or shoulder, and stop without blocking an intersection
Stop immediately where you are, even in an intersection
questions.explain: Pull to the shoulder or as far right as possible and stop, taking care not to block an intersection or endanger others.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Laws Governing Right-of-Way'

questions.q: Your light turns green but cars are still in the intersection. What should you do?
options: Wait until the intersection is clear before entering
Go immediately; you have the right-of-way
Go around the cars on the shoulder
questions.explain: Do not proceed 'just because' you have a green light; wait until the intersection is clear of traffic.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Laws Governing Right-of-Way'

questions.q: Another driver tries to take your turn at an intersection even though you have the right-of-way. What should you do?
options: Let the other driver go to avoid a crash
Proceed anyway since you have the right-of-way
Follow closely behind them through the intersection
questions.explain: Right-of-way is given, not taken. Letting the other driver proceed may prevent a crash.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Laws Governing Right-of-Way'

questions.q: In Georgia, when may you turn right on a red light?
options: Without stopping if no cars are coming
Only when a green arrow is showing
After a complete stop, yielding to traffic and pedestrians, unless a sign prohibits it
questions.explain: Right on red is allowed unless posted otherwise, but only after a full stop and yielding to all traffic and pedestrians.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Laws Governing Right-of-Way'

questions.q: When is a left turn on red allowed in Georgia?
options: From the left lane of a one-way street onto a one-way street whose traffic moves to the left, after stopping
Only from a center turn lane
From any street onto a two-way street after stopping
questions.explain: Unless a sign prohibits it, you may turn left on red from a one-way street onto a one-way street going left, after a complete stop and yielding.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Laws Governing Right-of-Way'

questions.q: When you approach a yield sign, you must:
options: Slow down, be ready to stop, and let other traffic go first
questions.explain: At a yield sign, slow to a safe speed and stop if needed; proceed only when it is safe.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Laws Governing Right-of-Way'

questions.q: Who has the right-of-way when you enter a roundabout?
options: Vehicles already circulating in the roundabout
questions.explain: When entering a roundabout you must yield to all circulating traffic, then merge into a gap.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Roundabouts'

questions.q: In which direction does traffic travel inside a roundabout?
options: Whichever way the first car goes
questions.explain: Traffic in a roundabout always circulates counterclockwise; you enter and exit to the right.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Roundabouts'

questions.q: In a multilane roundabout, which of these is correct?
options: Stop inside the roundabout to let cars enter
Change lanes freely to reach your exit
Choose your lane before entering and do not change lanes inside
Always use the outer lane to turn left
questions.explain: Get into the correct lane before entering, maintain your lane, and do not change lanes in the roundabout.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Roundabouts: Navigating a Multilane Roundabout'

questions.q: A school bus has stopped with red lights flashing and stop arm out on a two-lane road. What must drivers do?
options: Traffic in both directions must stop
Only traffic behind the bus must stop
Drivers may pass slowly at 10 mph
questions.explain: On a two-lane road, all traffic from both directions must stop for a school bus loading or unloading passengers.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Sharing the Road With School Buses'

questions.q: A school bus stops to load children on a four-lane road with no median. Which drivers must stop?
options: Only traffic in the lane next to the bus
No one, if the children are on the sidewalk
questions.explain: On a four-lane road without a median separation, all traffic from both directions must stop.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Sharing the Road With School Buses'

questions.q: A school bus stops on a road with a center turning lane. Who must stop?
options: Only traffic going the opposite way
Only traffic in the turning lane
questions.explain: A center turn lane is not a median; with a turning lane, all traffic in both directions must stop.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Sharing the Road With School Buses'

questions.q: On a divided highway of four or more lanes with a median, a school bus stops on the other side. What must you do?
options: You must stop until the bus moves
You must stop only if children are crossing
You are not required to stop, but watch for children
questions.explain: On a highway divided by a median, only traffic following the bus must stop; oncoming traffic should still watch for children.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Sharing the Road With School Buses'

questions.q: After stopping for a school bus, you may go again when:
options: The stop arm starts to fold, even if children are crossing
The bus moves or turns off its warning signals and all children have cleared the roadway
questions.explain: Stay stopped until the bus resumes motion or deactivates its signals AND all loading or unloading passengers are off the roadway.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Sharing the Road With School Buses'

questions.q: What do flashing yellow lights on a school bus mean?
options: The bus is preparing to stop; slow down and be ready to stop
questions.explain: Flashing yellow lights mean the bus is about to stop to load or unload; slow down and watch for children.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Laws Governing Right-of-Way'

questions.q: In a highway work zone, vehicles with flashing or revolving amber lights:
options: Can be passed at normal speed
Are only parked and can be ignored
questions.explain: Work vehicles and equipment with amber lights must be given the right-of-way; reduce speed as you approach.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Highway Work Zones: Yield to Amber Lights in Work Zones'

questions.q: A pedestrian who is blind and carrying a white cane or using a guide dog is crossing. You must:
options: Yield the right-of-way at all times
Yield only in a marked crosswalk
questions.explain: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes must be given the right-of-way at all times.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Blind Pedestrians'

questions.q: At a crosswalk without a signal, when must you stop and remain stopped for a pedestrian?
options: When the pedestrian is on your half of the road or within one lane of it
Only if a police officer is present
Only when the pedestrian is directly in front of your car
questions.explain: Stop and stay stopped when the pedestrian is on the half of the roadway you are on, or approaching and within one lane of it.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Respect Crosswalks'

questions.q: Where do crosswalks exist at intersections?
options: Only where there is a walk signal
On all four corners, even if they are not painted
questions.explain: Crosswalks exist at all four corners of intersections even when unmarked; marked mid-block crosswalks also exist.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Crosswalks'

questions.q: You are turning on a green light and pedestrians are crossing the street you are turning onto. You must:
options: Turn behind them while they are still in your lane
Turn ahead of them since you have a green light
Stop and remain stopped until they clear your lanes
questions.explain: The Walk signal usually runs with your green, so stop for pedestrians in the crosswalk of the road you are turning onto.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Watching for Pedestrians When Making Turns'

questions.q: A vehicle ahead of you in the next lane has stopped at a crosswalk. What should you do?
options: Do not pass it; a pedestrian may be crossing
Pass it carefully on the left
Pass it quickly before the pedestrian appears
questions.explain: It is illegal to overtake and pass a vehicle stopped to let a pedestrian cross at a marked or unmarked crosswalk.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Passing Stopped Cars'

questions.q: When entering an expressway from an acceleration lane, who has the right-of-way?
questions.explain: Vehicles on the expressway have the right-of-way; adjust speed in the acceleration lane and merge when safe.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Entering Expressways'

questions.q: Whose directions take priority over traffic lights and signs?
options: The traffic signal always takes priority
A law enforcement officer or firefighter directing traffic
The driver with the largest vehicle
questions.explain: One of the three most basic laws: obey an officer or firefighter's directions even when they conflict with traffic control devices.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': '3 Most Basic Traffic Laws'

questions.q: Unless another limit is posted, what is the maximum speed in an urban or residential district in Georgia?
questions.explain: Georgia's general limit in any urban or residential district is 30 mph unless posted otherwise.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Speed Limits'

questions.q: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit on an unpaved county road in Georgia?
questions.explain: The general limit on an unpaved county road is 35 mph.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Speed Limits'

questions.q: What is the general maximum speed on a rural interstate in Georgia unless posted otherwise?
questions.explain: Georgia's general limit on rural interstates is 70 mph.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Speed Limits'

questions.q: Unless posted otherwise, what is the maximum speed on an urban interstate or a multi-lane divided highway in Georgia?
questions.explain: The general limit is 65 mph on urban interstates and multi-lane divided highways.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Speed Limits'

questions.q: Where no other limit applies or is posted, Georgia's default maximum speed is:
questions.explain: In all other areas not covered by a specific rule, the general limit is 55 mph.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Speed Limits'

questions.q: Georgia's 'Super Speeder' fee applies to a driver convicted of going:
options: 20 mph or more over any limit
75 mph or more on a two-lane road, or 85 mph or more on any road
65 mph or more on any road
80 mph or more on an interstate only
questions.explain: Super Speeder applies to 75+ mph on a two-lane road or 85+ mph on any Georgia road.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Super Speeder'

questions.q: How much is Georgia's state Super Speeder fee, added to any local fine?
questions.explain: A $200 state fee is assessed in addition to local fines. Not paying on time leads to suspension and a $50 reinstatement fee.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Super Speeder'

questions.q: What happens if you do not pay the Super Speeder fee on time?
options: Your license is suspended and an extra $50 reinstatement fee applies
The fee is waived after 90 days
questions.explain: Failure to pay the state fee on time results in a license suspension and an additional $50 reinstatement fee.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Super Speeder'

questions.q: Which following-distance check does the Georgia manual recommend?
options: Stay at least 50 feet back at all speeds
Keep the car ahead's rear tires visible
Keep one car length for every 20 mph
Count 'one-thousand-one, one-thousand-two' after the car ahead passes a fixed point
questions.explain: Use a reference point and count two seconds; if you reach the point before you finish counting, you are too close.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Following Too Closely'

questions.q: When should you leave more than the normal following distance?
options: Only when your car is loaded
In bad weather, heavy traffic, construction and always at night
questions.explain: Increase the gap during inclement weather, construction, heavy traffic, and always at night.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Following Too Closely'

questions.q: How much following distance should you allow behind a motorcycle?
questions.explain: Allow more following distance, three or four seconds, so the rider can maneuver or stop in an emergency.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Sharing the Road With Motorcycles: Following Too Close'

questions.q: Georgia's law against driving too slowly can result in:
options: A fine up to $1,000 and/or 3 points
Loss of license for one year
questions.explain: Impeding the normal flow of traffic, including staying in the passing lane when overtaken, can bring a fine up to $1,000 and/or 3 points.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Driving Too Slowly'

questions.q: If you cannot keep up with a posted minimum speed on a highway, you should:
options: Turn on hazard lights and continue
questions.explain: Minimum speeds are posted on certain highways; if you cannot drive at the minimum, seek an alternate route.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Driving Too Slowly'

questions.q: Under Georgia's 'Slow Poke' law, a driver in the left (passing) lane who is being overtaken by faster traffic must:
options: Move right to let faster traffic pass, regardless of their own speed
Brake to warn the driver behind
Speed up to match the faster vehicle
Stay in the lane if driving at the speed limit
questions.explain: Slower drivers must move out of the passing lane when faster traffic approaches, whatever speed they are going, except in listed situations.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Keep Right, Except to Pass'

questions.q: Which is an exception to Georgia's 'keep right except to pass' rule?
options: You must use the left lane to exit or turn left
You are driving at the speed limit
questions.explain: Exceptions include traffic or weather conditions, exiting or turning left, paying a toll, and emergency or road-work vehicles.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Keep Right, Except to Pass'

questions.q: Disobeying a regulatory speed limit in a work zone can result in a fine of:
options: $100 to $2,000, up to 12 months in jail, or both
questions.explain: Work-zone speeding is a high and aggravated misdemeanor: a fine of $100 to $2,000 and/or up to 12 months imprisonment.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Highway Work Zones: Reduce Your Speed'

questions.q: In a work zone where no reduced speed limit is posted, you should:
options: Obey the normal posted limit but drive with extra caution
Drive 10 mph below the limit by law
questions.explain: If the limit is not reduced, obey the normal posted limit, but be more careful about conditions, lane position and workers.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Highway Work Zones: Reduce Your Speed'

questions.q: Black-on-orange advisory speed signs in a work zone:
options: Mean the work zone has ended
Suggest a safe speed and are used with warning signs
questions.explain: Advisory speeds are black and orange; official speed limit reductions use the standard black and white speed limit signs.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Highway Work Zones: Reduce Your Speed'

questions.q: To avoid 'overdriving' your headlights at night, you should:
options: Drive slowly enough to stop within the distance your headlights light up
Use high beams at all times
questions.explain: Do not drive at a speed that needs more stopping distance than your headlights illuminate.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Night Driving'

questions.q: At about what speed can partial hydroplaning begin in a standard passenger car?
questions.explain: Partial hydroplaning can start at around 35 mph, and by 55 mph the tires can lose contact with the road entirely.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Hydroplaning'

questions.q: If you realize you are going too fast in the middle of a curve, you should:
options: Ease off the accelerator, brake carefully, and keep steering in your lane
questions.explain: Reduce speed before curves. If already in one too fast, take your foot off the gas, brake carefully and keep steering; hard braking may cause a skid.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Curves'

questions.q: When a pedestrian is hit by a vehicle going 40 mph, the risk of death is about:
questions.explain: The manual's vehicle speed chart shows at least an 80% risk of pedestrian death at 40 mph.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Vehicle Speed'

questions.q: Compared with a car, how much distance does a fully loaded tractor-trailer at 55 mph need to stop?
questions.explain: A fully loaded tractor-trailer at 55 mph needs about three times the distance a car needs to stop.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Sharing the Road With Commercial Motor Vehicles'

questions.q: When passing on a two-lane road, you must be completely back in the right lane before oncoming traffic comes within:
questions.explain: You need enough time and space to return to the right lane before oncoming traffic is within 200 feet of your vehicle.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Passing: How To Pass On A Two-Lane Road'

questions.q: On a two-lane road, passing is prohibited within how many feet of a railroad crossing?
questions.explain: Passing is not allowed within 100 feet of a railroad crossing.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Passing is prohibited on two-lane roads'

questions.q: On a two-lane road, you may not pass within 100 feet of:
questions.explain: Passing is prohibited within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct or tunnel, and within 100 feet of a railroad crossing.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Passing is prohibited on two-lane roads'

questions.q: Which of these is a place where passing is NOT allowed on a two-lane road?
options: On a straight road with a broken yellow line and clear view
When the vehicle ahead is going well below the limit with a clear road ahead
Where the line on your side is broken
On a hill or curve where you cannot see oncoming traffic
questions.explain: You may not pass on a hill or curve where you cannot see oncoming vehicles that may be close enough to be a hazard.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Passing is prohibited on two-lane roads'

questions.q: Is it legal to pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder?
options: No, passing on the shoulder is prohibited
Yes, if the car ahead is turning left
Yes, if the shoulder is paved
questions.explain: Passing on the shoulder of the road is prohibited.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Passing is prohibited on two-lane roads'

questions.q: When may you pass another vehicle on the right?
options: Whenever the car ahead is slow
When it is turning left and there is enough pavement, or on a road with two or more lanes in your direction
On the shoulder if it is paved
questions.explain: Passing on the right is allowed beside a left-turning vehicle with enough pavement width, or on multi-lane roads going your way.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Passing On The Right'

questions.q: When you have finished passing, when should you return to the right lane?
options: When the other driver flashes headlights
When you can see the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror
As soon as your front bumper clears it
questions.explain: Do not return until you are safely clear; wait until you can see the car you passed in your rearview mirror, and signal right.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Passing: How To Pass On A Two-Lane Road'

questions.q: Another vehicle is passing you. What does the law say?
options: You must speed up to help it pass faster
You must pull onto the shoulder
You must not speed up until it has completely passed
questions.explain: It is unlawful to increase your speed before the overtaking vehicle has passed you completely; slowing slightly is courteous.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'When Someone Passes You'

questions.q: Flashing your turn signal to tell a driver behind you that it is safe to pass is:
questions.explain: Georgia law forbids using your turn signals as a courtesy 'go ahead and pass' signal to drivers behind you.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Illegal Signals'

questions.q: Weaving from lane to lane to move faster than traffic is:
options: Allowed if you signal each time
questions.explain: It is unlawful to weave between lanes to move faster than the flow of traffic.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Weaving'

questions.q: When making a right turn, you should approach the turn:
options: In the right lane, as close as practical to the curb or road edge
From the center of the road
From any lane if you signal
questions.explain: Signal, then approach in the right lane close to the curb, and finish in the right lane of the new street.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'How To Make A Right Turn'

questions.q: You are about to turn right across a bicycle lane. A cyclist is going straight through the intersection. You must:
options: Yield to the cyclist before turning
Turn first since cars have priority
Speed up to turn ahead of the cyclist
questions.explain: If there is a bicycle lane, yield to bicyclists going straight before making a right turn.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'How To Make A Right Turn'

questions.q: While waiting to turn left, how should you keep your front wheels?
options: Turned left so you are ready
Straight until you begin the turn
questions.explain: Keep wheels straight; if hit from behind, turned wheels could push you into oncoming traffic.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'How To Make A Left Turn'

questions.q: When turning left from a two-way street onto a multi-lane street, you should end the turn in:
options: The lane closest to the center line in your direction
questions.explain: Finish a left turn in the lane closest to the center (or center line) in your direction on the new street.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'How To Make A Left Turn'

questions.q: If there are two left-turn lanes, a driver in the second (outer) turn lane should finish the turn in:
options: The right lane, then change lanes
The corresponding lane on the new street
questions.explain: With multiple turning lanes, complete the turn into the corresponding lane on the street you are entering.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'How To Make A Left Turn'

questions.q: Once you have entered an intersection to make a left turn, can you change lanes in the intersection?
options: Yes, if no cars are near
questions.explain: Once in the intersection to turn left, you may not change lanes within it.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'How To Make A Left Turn'

questions.q: Where should you avoid making a U-turn?
options: At an intersection where it is allowed and safe
On a curve or near the top of a hill where others cannot see you
On a wide residential street with clear views
questions.explain: Do not U-turn on a curve or near a hilltop where drivers from either direction cannot see you, or where signs prohibit it.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'U-Turns'

questions.q: You must give a turn signal:
options: Continuously for an adequate distance before every turn
Only when other cars are present
questions.explain: A continuous turn signal must be given for an adequate distance before any right or left turn.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Turn Signals and Making Turns Safely'

questions.q: Which hand-and-arm signal means a left turn?
options: Right arm out the passenger window
questions.explain: A left turn is shown with the left arm straight out; arm up means right turn, arm down means stop or slow.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Turn Signals and Making Turns Safely'

questions.q: Which hand-and-arm signal means a right turn?
options: Left arm bent upward at the elbow
questions.explain: Right turn: left arm bent up at the elbow. Stop or slow: left arm bent down.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Turn Signals and Making Turns Safely'

questions.q: A hand-and-arm signal with the left arm pointing downward means the driver is:
questions.explain: The left arm bent downward signals a stop or a decrease in speed.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Turn Signals and Making Turns Safely'

questions.q: On a multi-lane two-way highway, when may you drive to the left of the center line?
options: Only when making a left turn or when signs or signals allow it
questions.explain: On a multi-lane two-way highway you must never cross to the left of center except to turn left or when authorized by signals or signs.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Making Turns on Multi-Lane Highways'

questions.q: On a two-way road with four or more lanes and two solid yellow center lines, you may cross the center lines:
options: Only to turn left into or from an alley, driveway, private road or street
questions.explain: Two solid yellow center lines on a four-plus-lane road may be crossed only when turning left into or out of a driveway, alley, private road or another street.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Pavement Markings: Lane Lines'

questions.q: When entering an expressway, the solid white lines of the 'gore' area between the acceleration lane and the travel lane:
options: May not be crossed; stay in the acceleration lane until the line ends
Show where to stop and wait
May be crossed if traffic is light
questions.explain: Drivers entering a controlled-access highway may not cross the solid white gore line and must continue in the acceleration lane until it disappears.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Gores'

questions.q: To exit an expressway on the right, you should:
options: Move into the right lane in advance and slow down in the deceleration lane
Stop on the shoulder and then exit
Cross several lanes at the last moment
Slow down sharply in the left lane
questions.explain: Move to the right lane early for a right exit and use the deceleration lane to slow down.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Exiting Expressways'

questions.q: If you miss your exit on an expressway, you should:
options: Back up carefully on the shoulder
Continue to the next exit; never back up
Stop and wait for a gap to reverse
Make a U-turn through the median
questions.explain: Backing up on a controlled-access roadway is prohibited under any circumstances, and crossing the median is unlawful except at authorized crossovers.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Controlled-Access Roadways'

questions.q: Before backing up, you should:
options: Open the door and look down
Check all around and look over your right shoulder, not just in mirrors
questions.explain: Check every side of the car first, then look back over your right shoulder as you reverse rather than relying on mirrors alone.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Backing Up'

questions.q: In Georgia, you may not park within how many feet of a fire hydrant?
questions.explain: Stopping or parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant is limited to momentarily picking up or dropping off passengers.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Stopping, Standing, and Parking'

questions.q: How close may you park to a crosswalk at an intersection in Georgia?
questions.explain: Parking within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection is not allowed (only momentary passenger pick-up or drop-off).
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Stopping, Standing, and Parking'

questions.q: You may not park within how many feet of a stop sign, yield sign or traffic signal?
questions.explain: The limit is 30 feet from a stop sign, yield sign or traffic control signal.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Stopping, Standing, and Parking'

questions.q: You may not park within how many feet of a railroad crossing?
questions.explain: Parking within 50 feet of a railroad crossing is not allowed.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Stopping, Standing, and Parking'

questions.q: On the same side of the street as a fire station driveway, you may not park within:
questions.explain: Do not park within 20 feet of a fire station driveway (or within 75 feet of the spot across the street from it).
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Stopping, Standing, and Parking'

questions.q: When parking on the opposite side of the street from a fire station driveway, you must stay at least:
options: 75 feet from the spot across from the driveway
questions.explain: Across the street from a fire station driveway, keep at least 75 feet from the point directly opposite the driveway.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Stopping, Standing, and Parking'

questions.q: Where is stopping, standing or parking NOT allowed at any time?
options: Along a curb 40 feet from a hydrant
In a driveway you own, off the street
questions.explain: You may never stop, stand or park on a bridge, overpass, or in a tunnel, among other places.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Stopping, Standing, and Parking'

questions.q: Double parking (stopping on the street side of a parked vehicle) is:
questions.explain: Stopping, standing or parking on the street side of any parked vehicle is prohibited at all times.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Stopping, Standing, and Parking'

questions.q: Which of these places is a prohibited parking location at all times?
options: In a marked space on a residential street
On the shoulder of your own private driveway
questions.explain: Parking on a sidewalk, within an intersection, on a crosswalk, on railroad tracks, or on a controlled-access roadway is never allowed.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Stopping, Standing, and Parking'

questions.q: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, you should try to park it off the road so that it can be seen from:
questions.explain: Get a disabled vehicle off the highway if at all possible, leaving traffic room to pass and keeping it visible from 200 feet away in both directions.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Stopping, Standing, and Parking'

questions.q: When you parallel park, you should begin by stopping beside the car in front of the space about how far from it?
questions.explain: Pull up even with the car ahead of the space, about 2 feet away, before backing in.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Steps to Parallel Parking'

questions.q: On the Georgia road test, a parallel-parked car must be no more than how far from the curb?
questions.explain: For the road test you must park midway between the standards and not more than 18 inches from the curb.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 3 'Testing Information': 'Road Test For Class C or D'

questions.q: You may not park a vehicle within how many feet of a fire truck stopped in answer to a fire alarm?
questions.explain: Do not park within 500 feet of fire apparatus stopped in answer to an alarm.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Following Emergency Vehicles'

questions.q: Before opening your car door on the traffic side, you must:
options: Make sure it is safe and will not interfere with traffic, including bicyclists
questions.explain: Opening a door on the traffic side is prohibited unless it is safe and does not interfere with other traffic, including cyclists near parked cars.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Opening Vehicle Doors'

questions.q: What is the minimum space Georgia law requires when passing a bicyclist?
questions.explain: If you cannot move to a non-adjacent lane, you must pass with at least three feet between your vehicle and the bicycle.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Important Reminders Concerning Bicycle Riders'

questions.q: If you cannot change lanes to pass a bicyclist, how fast may you go when passing?
options: At least 10 mph under the posted limit or 25 mph, whichever is more
questions.explain: Slow to a speed at least 10 mph below the limit or 25 mph, whichever is greater, and keep 3 feet of space.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Important Reminders Concerning Bicycle Riders'

questions.q: Violating Georgia's safe-passing law for bicycles is a misdemeanor with a fine of up to:
questions.explain: A violation of the bicycle passing law is punishable by a fine up to $250.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Important Reminders Concerning Bicycle Riders'

questions.q: On which roads in Georgia are bicyclists NOT allowed?
questions.explain: Bicyclists may use every Georgia road except interstates and limited-access highways.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Sharing the Road With Bicycles'

questions.q: A bicyclist is riding in the middle of the lane even though a bike lane is nearby. This is:
options: Illegal unless the cyclist is turning
Legal; cyclists may use the full lane and are not required to use the bike lane
Illegal; cyclists must use the bike lane
questions.explain: Georgia law allows bicyclists to use the full lane, and they are not required to ride in a bike lane even when one exists.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Sharing the Road With Bicycles'

questions.q: May a car drive or park in a bicycle lane?
options: Yes, if no bicycles are present
No, except to cross it to make a turn, yielding to bicyclists
questions.explain: Motorists may not drive or park in a bike lane except to cross it for a turn, and must yield to cyclists when doing so.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Pavement Markings: Bicycle Lanes'

questions.q: You meet a bicyclist at night while your high beams are on. You should:
options: Keep high beams on so the cyclist can see
questions.explain: Dim your lights for an oncoming bicyclist to avoid blinding the rider.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Important Reminders Concerning Bicycle Riders'

questions.q: Where is a bicycle lane placed when there is a right-turn-only lane?
options: To the left of the right-turn-only lane
In the center of the road
To the right of the turn lane, next to the curb
questions.explain: With a right-turn-only lane, the bike lane is to its left so straight-through cyclists are not in the turning path.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 7 'Signs, Signals & Markings': 'Pavement Markings: Bicycle Lanes'

questions.q: When passing a motorcyclist, you must:
options: Pass within the same lane if there is room
Pass using the adjacent lane and never share the motorcycle's lane
questions.explain: A motorcycle is entitled to the full width of a lane; drivers may not occupy the same lane while passing.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Passing Motorcyclists'

questions.q: Why might a motorcyclist change position within a lane?
options: Because they want you to pass in the same lane
To be seen more easily or avoid road hazards
Because they are about to stop
questions.explain: Riders adjust lane position for visibility and to avoid debris, potholes and other hazards, not to be reckless.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Sharing the Road With Motorcycles: Allow a Full Lane'

questions.q: Where are car-motorcycle crashes most likely to happen?
questions.explain: Intersections are the most likely place, usually because a driver fails to see the motorcycle and turns into its path.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Sharing the Road With Motorcycles: Intersections'

questions.q: A motorcycle's turn signal is flashing as it approaches an intersection. You should:
options: Wait to be sure the rider is actually turning before you proceed
Assume it is turning and pull out
questions.explain: Motorcycle signals may not self-cancel; do not assume the rider will turn until the maneuver has clearly started.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Sharing the Road With Motorcycles: Intersections'

questions.q: If you cannot see a truck driver's face in the truck's side mirror:
options: The truck driver cannot see you
You are in the best place to pass
The driver can see you through the rear window
You are at a safe distance
questions.explain: Trucks have large side No-Zones; if you can't see the driver's face in the mirror, the driver can't see you.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Sharing the Road With Commercial Motor Vehicles'

questions.q: Which side No-Zone of a truck is especially dangerous?
options: The right side, because trucks make wide right turns
There are no side blind spots on trucks
questions.explain: Trucks and buses swing wide to make right turns, so their right-side blind spot is the most dangerous place to be.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Sharing the Road With Commercial Motor Vehicles'

questions.q: After passing a large truck, it is safe to move back in front of it when:
options: Your rear bumper clears its front bumper
You are one car length ahead
You can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror
questions.explain: To avoid the Front No-Zone, make sure you can see the whole front of the truck in your rearview mirror before pulling in.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Sharing the Road With Commercial Motor Vehicles'

questions.q: Why is following a large truck closely dangerous?
options: It is only dangerous at night
It improves your fuel mileage, which is safe
The truck has a big rear blind spot and blocks your view of traffic ahead
questions.explain: Trucks have huge rear No-Zones and no rearview mirror; tailgating also hides traffic ahead from you.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Sharing the Road With Commercial Motor Vehicles'

questions.q: Georgia's TACT guidance suggests, when pulling in front of a truck, leaving at least:
options: One car length for every 10 mph of speed
Half a car length per 10 mph
One car length at any speed
questions.explain: Don't cut off commercial vehicles; one car length for every 10 mph of speed is recommended.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Sharing the Road With Commercial Motor Vehicles'

questions.q: Under Georgia's Move Over law, when you approach an emergency, sanitation or utility vehicle stopped on the shoulder with flashing lights, you must:
options: Maintain speed and stay in your lane
Move over a lane if safe; if not, slow below the speed limit and be ready to stop
Stop in your lane until it leaves
questions.explain: Move to the next lane if safely possible; if you cannot, slow down below the speed limit and be prepared to stop.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'The "Move Over" Law'

questions.q: The maximum fine for a first violation of Georgia's Move Over law is:
questions.explain: A first Move Over violation can bring a fine of no more than $500.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'The "Move Over" Law'

questions.q: You approach a postal vehicle or active sanitation truck with flashing lights and cannot change lanes. You must:
options: Slow to at least 10 mph under the limit or 25 mph, whichever is more, and be ready to stop
Use the center turn lane to pass
questions.explain: If a lane change is not possible, reduce to at least 10 mph below the limit or 25 mph, whichever is greater, and prepare to stop.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Passing a Postal Carrier or Sanitation Workers'

questions.q: When stopping at a crosswalk on a multi-lane road, how far back should you stop so drivers in other lanes can see the pedestrian?
options: At least 2 feet before the crosswalk
At least 10 feet before the crosswalk
questions.explain: On a multi-lane road, stop 10 feet or more back from the crosswalk so drivers in the next lane can still see the pedestrian.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Passing Stopped Cars in Lanes of Travel'

questions.q: When turning right on red, after looking left for a gap in traffic, you should also:
options: Move into the crosswalk to see better
Look right to make sure no pedestrian is crossing in front of you
questions.explain: Stop before the crosswalk, check left for traffic, then look to your passenger side for pedestrians before turning.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Turning Right at a Red Traffic Signal'

questions.q: When leaving a driveway or parking garage that crosses a sidewalk, you must:
options: Sound your horn and drive out
Stop before the sidewalk and go only after pedestrians have passed
questions.explain: Drivers exiting or entering driveways, alleys or garages must stop before the sidewalk area and let pedestrians pass.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Exiting and Entering Driveways'

questions.q: Drivers of trucks or vehicles pulling trailers outside business or residential districts must:
options: Leave enough space so an overtaking vehicle can safely move in between them
Travel close together in a group
questions.explain: Trucks and trailers must leave sufficient space between each other; 'caravanning' is prohibited.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Trucks and Vehicles Pulling Trailers'

questions.q: Can passengers ride in a house trailer while it is being towed on a Georgia highway?
options: Yes, if they wear seat belts
questions.explain: Riding in a house trailer or any towed trailer on a street or highway is not allowed.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Riding in Trailers'

questions.q: What is the maximum trailer width allowed on Georgia highways?
questions.explain: Georgia does not allow trailers more than 8 feet 6 inches wide on its highways.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Trucks and Vehicles Pulling Trailers'

questions.q: You may not follow a fire truck responding to an alarm closer than:
questions.explain: Unless on official business, do not follow fire apparatus or other emergency vehicles responding to an emergency closer than 200 feet.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Following Emergency Vehicles'

questions.q: A flagger in a work zone signals you to stop. The flagger's signal has:
options: Less authority than a warning sign
The same authority as a regulatory sign
questions.explain: A flagger directing traffic in a work zone carries the same legal weight as a regulatory sign, so you must follow the flagger's signals.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Highway Work Zones: Obey Flaggers'

questions.q: Slow mobile work vehicles (such as paint stripers) with flashing amber lights may travel at about:
options: 5 mph; slow down, yield, and follow their directions
questions.explain: Mobile work vehicles usually move very slowly, such as 5 mph; slow down, yield and follow any displayed directions.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Highway Work Zones: Yield to Mobile Work Vehicles'

questions.q: When workers are close to an open lane in a work zone, you should:
options: Change lanes away from them or shift within your lane to add space
Drive closer to the workers to avoid the cones
questions.explain: Move away from workers when lanes are narrowed, or shift within your lane to give them more room.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Highway Work Zones: Adjust Your Lane Position'

questions.q: Which vehicles may use Georgia HOV lanes?
options: Vehicles with more than one occupant, buses, motorcycles and AFV-plated vehicles
questions.explain: HOV lanes are restricted to vehicles with more than one occupant, buses, motorcycles and Alternative Fuel Vehicles with proper plates.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'HOV Lanes'

questions.q: Between what times must you use your headlights in Georgia?
options: From one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise
From one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise
questions.explain: Headlights are required from half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise, any time it is raining, and when visibility is limited.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Use Headlights Properly'

questions.q: Georgia law requires headlights whenever:
questions.explain: You must use your headlights any time it is raining, as well as at night and when visibility is limited.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Use Headlights Properly'

questions.q: You must dim your high beams when an oncoming vehicle is within:
questions.explain: Dim your headlights within 500 feet of an approaching vehicle so you do not blind its driver.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Use Headlights Properly'

questions.q: You should use low beams when following another vehicle within:
questions.explain: Dim your lights when following closely, within 200 feet, behind another vehicle.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Use Headlights Properly'

questions.q: When driving in heavy fog, you should:
options: Use high beams to see farther
Slow down and use low-beam headlights
questions.explain: High beams cause glare in fog. Reduce speed, dim headlights, and do not drive with parking or hazard lights on.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Fog'

questions.q: If your car starts to skid, you should first:
options: Ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction of the skid
Steer the opposite way of the skid
questions.explain: Take your foot off the gas and steer in the direction of the skid; once in control, brake lightly and steer to safety.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Skidding'

questions.q: Why is the first half-hour of rain especially dangerous?
options: Water mixes with oil on the road and makes it very slippery
questions.explain: The first half-hour of rain is most dangerous because water mixes with oil and chemicals on the pavement.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Skidding'

questions.q: If your car begins to hydroplane, you should:
options: Take your foot off the accelerator and let the car slow down
questions.explain: When hydroplaning, ease off the accelerator and let the car slow; slowing down on wet roads helps prevent it.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Hydroplaning'

questions.q: If your wheels drift off the pavement onto the shoulder, you should:
options: Ease off the gas, brake gently, and return to the road only when slowed and safe
Jerk the wheel to get back on quickly
questions.explain: Don't panic or overcorrect. Slow down, check traffic, then return carefully; jerking the wheel can cause a skid or rollover.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Leaving the Roadway'

questions.q: Where should your hands generally be on the steering wheel?
options: At 10 and 2 with thumbs inside the wheel
At about 9 o'clock and 3 o'clock (or 8 and 4 if the manufacturer recommends)
questions.explain: The manual recommends 9 and 3; some manufacturers suggest 8 and 4 with air bags.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Steering'

questions.q: Using the 'penny test,' your tire tread is too worn when:
options: Part of Lincoln's head is covered
You can see all of Lincoln's head
The penny fits tightly in the groove
questions.explain: If any part of Lincoln's head is covered, tread is adequate; below about 2/32 inch, grip is greatly reduced.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Tire Pressure'

questions.q: Symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning include:
options: Sudden weariness, yawning, dizziness and nausea
questions.explain: Carbon monoxide is odorless and colorless; signs include sudden weariness, yawning, dizziness and nausea.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Carbon Monoxide'

questions.q: Which action helps prevent carbon monoxide poisoning?
options: Run the heater while parked with windows up
Keep the windows closed while idling
Never run the engine in a closed garage
questions.explain: Don't run the engine in a garage, don't idle with windows closed, and keep the exhaust system in good repair.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Carbon Monoxide'

questions.q: What happens if you turn the ignition to the 'lock' position while the car is moving?
options: The steering locks and you cannot steer
questions.explain: With a steering lock, turning the key to lock while moving disables steering.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Steering Locks'

questions.q: To stay alert on a long expressway trip and avoid 'highway hypnosis,' you should:
options: Keep your eyes moving and stop if you feel drowsy
questions.explain: Shift your eyes often, talk with passengers, and stop when drowsy; stimulant drugs make driving more hazardous.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Tips For Expressway Driving'
