questions.q: Stopping on the shoulder of an expressway is allowed:
options: To get something from the back seat
questions.explain: Stopping on the shoulder is permitted only in an emergency; switching drivers or retrieving items is not an emergency.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Tips For Expressway Driving'

questions.q: If your vehicle has trouble and you must stop on an expressway shoulder, you should:
options: Walk along the expressway to find help
Leave the car in a travel lane
Stand behind the car in traffic
Raise the hood and turn on your hazard lights
questions.explain: Raise the hood and turn on hazard lights to signal trouble; do not walk along the expressway looking for help.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Tips For Expressway Driving'

questions.q: Coasting down a hill with the transmission in neutral is:
questions.explain: Drivers must not coast downhill with the gears or transmission in neutral.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Coasting'

questions.q: Wearing headphones or a headset that blocks your hearing while driving is:
options: Legal if the volume is low
questions.explain: It is unlawful to drive while wearing headphones or a headset that impairs your ability to hear.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Impaired Hearing and Vision'

questions.q: Under Georgia's Hands-Free law, which is allowed while driving?
options: Using a phone in a mount or by voice/hands-free
Reading a text at a red light while holding the phone
Holding the phone to make a call
Watching a video on a mounted phone
questions.explain: Drivers may not hold or support a phone; it may be used only with a hands-free device or mount, and videos may not be watched.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Texting & Cell Phones'

questions.q: What is the penalty for a first conviction under Georgia's Hands-Free law?
options: 1 point and a fine of not more than $50
questions.explain: First conviction: 1 point and up to $50. Second: 2 points and up to $100. Third or more: 3 points and up to $150.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Texting & Cell Phones'

questions.q: A third or later Hands-Free law conviction brings:
options: 3 points and a fine of up to $150
questions.explain: Third and subsequent convictions carry 3 points and a fine of no more than $150.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Texting & Cell Phones'

questions.q: Under Georgia law as described in the manual, who must wear a seat belt?
options: Everyone in the front seat, and all occupants under 18 in any seat
questions.explain: Every front-seat occupant must be belted, and all occupants under 18 must be belted wherever they sit.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Safety Belts'

questions.q: Georgia has a 'primary' safety belt law. This means:
options: You can only be cited after a crash
Only the driver can be cited
Officers can stop and cite you for not wearing a belt alone
questions.explain: A primary law lets officers stop and cite violators without seeing another violation.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Safety Belts'

questions.q: Children under what age must ride in an appropriate child restraint system in Georgia?
questions.explain: A child under eight must be properly restrained in a child passenger restraint suitable for the child's height and weight.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Safety Restraints for Children'

questions.q: A first conviction for failing to properly restrain a child is worth how many points?
questions.explain: Child Restraint first offense: 1 point; second and later: 2 points.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 10 'Losing Your Driving Privileges': 'Violations and points demerited'

questions.q: Driving across a median strip at a place other than an authorized crossover is:
questions.explain: It is unlawful to cross a dividing section, barrier or unpaved strip except at an authorized opening.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Median Strip'

questions.q: What are the three most basic traffic laws in Georgia?
options: Obey traffic devices, obey officers and firefighters directing traffic, and never drive on a closed road
Carry a license, insurance, and registration
questions.explain: The manual lists these three basic laws: obey traffic control devices, obey officer/firefighter directions, and never drive on a closed roadway.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': '3 Most Basic Traffic Laws'

questions.q: Throwing litter from a vehicle in Georgia can result in:
options: A fine up to $1,000, up to 12 months in jail, and possibly picking up litter
questions.explain: Littering is a misdemeanor; penalties can include up to $1,000, 12 months in jail, and court-ordered litter pickup. The driver is responsible for litter thrown from the vehicle.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Georgia's Litter Control Law'

questions.q: Overloading a vehicle so that passengers or cargo block the driver's view is:
questions.explain: A vehicle loaded so as to obstruct the driver's view or controls cannot legally be driven.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Obstructing the Driver's View'

questions.q: A defensive driver should:
options: Follow closely to keep traffic moving
Never assume other drivers will do what you expect and always have an escape route
questions.explain: Defensive driving means awareness: keep your eyes moving, check mirrors, and plan an escape route; a turn signal doesn't guarantee a turn.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Tips For Expressway Driving'

questions.q: When visibility is greatly reduced at night, what can help you stay in your lane?
options: Driving in the middle of two lanes
Following the right edge line (or the center line if there is no edge line)
questions.explain: Use the edge line as a guide; if there is none, use the center line.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Night Driving'

questions.q: During which months are deer most active and most likely to cause crashes in Georgia?
questions.explain: Deer are most active during the October–December breeding season; late February and early March are also critical.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 11 'Crashes': 'Deer-Automobile Crashes'

questions.q: A deer suddenly runs in front of your car. What should you do?
options: Slow down as much as possible but do not swerve
Speed up so it runs away
questions.explain: Never swerve to avoid a deer; it can cause you to hit another vehicle or leave the road. Brake to reduce impact.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 11 'Crashes': 'Deer-Automobile Crashes'

questions.q: You see a deer beside the road at night. You should:
options: Slow down, blink your lights and use low beams
Keep high beams on to freeze it
Stop in the travel lane and wait
questions.explain: Slow immediately, blink your headlights and switch to low beam so you do not blind the deer; short horn blasts may help.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 11 'Crashes': 'Deer-Automobile Crashes'

questions.q: A driver age 21 or older is considered 'under the influence' in Georgia at a blood alcohol concentration of:
questions.explain: For drivers 21 and older, 0.08 grams or more is the legal limit.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Driving Under the Influence of Drugs or Alcohol'

questions.q: A driver under 21 is considered 'under the influence' in Georgia at a blood alcohol concentration of:
questions.explain: Drivers under 21 are irrefutably considered under the influence at 0.02 grams or more.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Driving Under the Influence of Drugs or Alcohol'

questions.q: What blood alcohol level disqualifies someone driving a commercial motor vehicle (CMV)?
questions.explain: Driving a CMV with a BAC of .04 or higher is a major traffic violation that disqualifies commercial privileges for one year.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 10 'Losing Your Driving Privileges': 'Major Traffic Violations'

questions.q: Having a valid prescription for a medicine that impairs your driving is:
options: Not a defense to a DUI charge
questions.explain: Having a prescription is not a defense if the medication impairs your ability to drive safely.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Driving Under the Influence of Drugs or Alcohol'

questions.q: According to the manual, a DUI conviction can bring:
options: Fines up to $1,000, jail up to 12 months, and mandatory license suspension
A warning on the first offense
questions.explain: DUI penalties are severe: fines up to $1,000, up to 12 months in jail, and mandatory suspension of driving privileges.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Driving Under the Influence of Drugs or Alcohol'

questions.q: Under Georgia's implied consent law, if you refuse state-administered chemical testing, your license will be suspended for at least:
questions.explain: Refusal results in a suspension of at least one year, and refusal of blood or urine testing may be used as evidence at trial.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 10 'Losing Your Driving Privileges': 'Implied Consent'

questions.q: Under implied consent, after taking the state's test you have the right to:
options: Refuse all further questions and keep driving
Additional tests at your own expense by qualified personnel you choose
A free attorney at the roadside
Have the state's result thrown out automatically
questions.explain: After submitting to the state tests, you may get additional chemical tests at your own expense from qualified personnel of your choosing.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 10 'Losing Your Driving Privileges': 'Implied Consent'

questions.q: A driver under 21 has a BAC of 0.02 or more but less than 0.08, with no prior serious convictions. The first DUI suspension is a minimum of:
questions.explain: For a first under-21 DUI with BAC .02 to under .08, the minimum suspension is 6 months (12 months with certain prior convictions).
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 6 'Teen Driving Laws': 'Convictions for Driving Under the Influence of Drugs or Alcohol (DUI)'

questions.q: A driver under 21 convicted of DUI with a BAC of 0.08 or more (or who refused testing) faces a minimum suspension of:
questions.explain: BAC .08 or more, or a test refusal, results in at least a 12-month suspension for an under-21 driver.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 6 'Teen Driving Laws': 'Convictions for Driving Under the Influence of Drugs or Alcohol (DUI)'

questions.q: Can a driver under 21 convicted of DUI get a limited driving permit?
questions.explain: No limited driving permit is available for DUI convictions prior to age 21.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 6 'Teen Driving Laws': 'Convictions for Driving Under the Influence of Drugs or Alcohol (DUI)'

questions.q: For a teen's second DUI, the license suspension is a minimum of:
options: 18 months, with ignition interlock permit eligibility after 120 days
questions.explain: A second DUI suspension lasts at least 18 months, with eligibility for an ignition interlock permit after 120 days.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 6 'Teen Driving Laws': 'Convictions for Driving Under the Influence of Drugs or Alcohol (DUI)'

questions.q: Possessing an open container of an alcoholic beverage while driving adds how many points?
questions.explain: An open container conviction carries 2 points.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 10 'Losing Your Driving Privileges': 'Violations and points demerited'

questions.q: A Georgia driver's license is suspended for points when an adult accumulates:
questions.explain: Accumulating 15 or more points within 24 months results in suspension.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 10 'Losing Your Driving Privileges': 'The Points System'

questions.q: A driver under 18 will have their license suspended for accumulating:
questions.explain: Drivers under 18 are suspended for 4 or more points within any 12-month period.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 10 'Losing Your Driving Privileges': 'The Points System'

questions.q: A driver under 21 is convicted of a single 4-point offense. What happens?
questions.explain: Any person under 21 convicted of a 4-point violation has their license suspended.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 10 'Losing Your Driving Privileges': 'The Points System'

questions.q: How many points are assessed for speeding 15 to 18 mph over the limit?
questions.explain: Speeding 15–18 mph over: 2 points; 19–23 over: 3 points; 24–33 over: 4 points; 34+ over: 6 points.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 10 'Losing Your Driving Privileges': 'Violations and points demerited'

questions.q: How many points are assessed for speeding 24 to 33 mph over the limit?
questions.explain: Speeding 24–33 mph over the posted limit is a 4-point offense, which also suspends the license of a driver under 21.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 10 'Losing Your Driving Privileges': 'Violations and points demerited'

questions.q: Speeding 34 mph or more over the limit carries how many points?
questions.explain: Speeding 34 mph or more over the posted limit is a 6-point offense.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 10 'Losing Your Driving Privileges': 'Violations and points demerited'

questions.q: Unlawfully passing a stopped school bus in Georgia can bring:
options: Up to a $1,000 fine and 6 points, with a mandatory court appearance
questions.explain: Penalties include a mandatory court appearance, a fine up to $1,000 and up to 6 points; drivers under 21 lose their license.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 9 'Sharing the Road': 'Sharing the Road With School Buses'

questions.q: How many points does a reckless driving conviction carry?
questions.explain: Reckless driving is a 4-point offense and also triggers suspension for drivers under 21.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 10 'Losing Your Driving Privileges': 'Violations and points demerited'

questions.q: Aggressive driving (driving with intent to annoy, harass, intimidate or obstruct someone) carries how many points?
questions.explain: Aggressive driving is a misdemeanor of a high and aggravated nature and carries 6 points.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 10 'Losing Your Driving Privileges': 'Violations and points demerited'

questions.q: Disobeying a traffic-control device or a traffic officer is worth how many points?
questions.explain: Disobedience of a traffic-control device or officer carries 3 points.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 10 'Losing Your Driving Privileges': 'Violations and points demerited'

questions.q: Improper passing on a hill or curve carries how many points?
questions.explain: Improper passing on a hill or curve is a 4-point violation.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 10 'Losing Your Driving Privileges': 'Violations and points demerited'

questions.q: How can a licensed Georgia driver have up to 7 points removed from their record?
options: Complete a certified 6-hour defensive driving course, once every 5 years
questions.explain: Completing a certified 6-hour driver improvement course allows a reduction of up to 7 points once every five years.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 10 'Losing Your Driving Privileges': 'Points Reduction'

questions.q: If you complete a certified defensive driving course before your court date for a moving violation, the court may:
options: Reduce your fine by 20% and assess no points (once every five years)
Give you a free license renewal
questions.explain: Under points avoidance, the court reduces the fine by 20% and assesses no points; this plea is allowed once every five years.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 10 'Losing Your Driving Privileges': 'Points Avoidance'

questions.q: For a driver under 21, which conviction results in a 6-month suspension for a first offense?
questions.explain: Under-21 drivers lose their license for 6 months (first) or 12 months (second) for offenses like reckless driving, racing or hit-and-run.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 6 'Teen Driving Laws': 'Convictions Other Than DUI'

questions.q: A driver under 21 convicted of speeding 24 mph or more over the limit will:
options: Pay a $25 fine with no other penalty
questions.explain: Speeding 24 mph or more over the limit leads to suspension for drivers under 21.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 10 'Losing Your Driving Privileges': 'Types of Suspensions'

questions.q: A person becomes a Habitual Violator in Georgia after how many convictions of serious offenses such as DUI within 5 years?
questions.explain: A third conviction of offenses like DUI, vehicular homicide or hit-and-run within 5 years results in Habitual Violator revocation.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 10 'Losing Your Driving Privileges': 'Mandatory Revocations'

questions.q: A first conviction for reckless stunt driving within 5 years results in a suspension of:
questions.explain: First conviction: 12-month suspension, with early reinstatement possible after 120 days.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Drag Racing/Reckless Stunt Driving'

questions.q: Racing on Georgia highways includes:
options: Speeding up to keep another driver from passing you
questions.explain: Racing includes competing with other drivers, trying to block a vehicle from passing by accelerating or maneuvering, or racing against time.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Racing'

questions.q: Driving without insurance in Georgia results in:
options: No penalty if you have no crash
questions.explain: DDS is required by law to suspend driving privileges for a conviction of driving without insurance.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 10 'Losing Your Driving Privileges': 'Types of Suspensions'

questions.q: What is the fee for a limited driving permit during an eligible suspension?
questions.explain: A limited driving permit may be available during some suspensions for a fee of $32.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 10 'Losing Your Driving Privileges': 'Limited Driving Permits'

questions.q: At what age can you apply for a Class CP instructional permit in Georgia?
questions.explain: Upon reaching age 15, or any time after, you may apply for a Class C Instructional Permit (CP).
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 6 'Teen Driving Laws': 'Obtaining a Class C Instructional Permit (CP)'

questions.q: A Class CP permit holder may drive only when accompanied by someone who is:
options: At least 21, licensed for Class C, fit to drive, and seated beside the driver
Any licensed adult in any seat
questions.explain: The supervisor must be at least 21, hold a Class C license, be fit and capable of controlling the vehicle, and sit in the front passenger seat.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 6 'Teen Driving Laws': 'Conditions of a Class C Instructional Permit (CP)'

questions.q: How long must a teen hold an instructional permit before applying for a Class D license at age 16?
questions.explain: You may apply for a Class D at 16 after holding a valid instructional permit for one year and one day.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 6 'Teen Driving Laws': 'Obtaining a Class D Provisional License'

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a 16- or 17-year-old complete for a Class D license?
options: At least 20 hours, including 2 at night
At least 40 hours, including 6 at night
At least 30 hours, none at night
At least 50 hours, including 10 at night
questions.explain: Teens need a cumulative total of at least 40 hours of driving experience, including at least 6 hours at night.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 6 'Teen Driving Laws': 'Driver Education Requirements'

questions.q: Under Joshua's Law, an approved driver education course includes:
options: 30 hours of classroom (or online) instruction plus 6 hours behind the wheel with an instructor or the Parent/Teen Driving Guide
questions.explain: The course is 30 classroom hours or an equivalent online course, plus 6 hours with a certified instructor or completion of the Parent/Teen Driving Guide.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 6 'Teen Driving Laws': 'Driver Education Requirements'

questions.q: What program must teens complete, in addition to driver education, to get a Class D license?
options: The Alcohol and Drug Awareness Program (ADAP)
questions.explain: Applicants under 18 must complete ADAP, taught in most schools and also available online.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 6 'Teen Driving Laws': 'Obtaining a Class D Provisional License'

questions.q: Class D provisional license holders may NOT drive during which hours?
options: 11:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. except for work
12:00 a.m. to 5:00 a.m., with no exceptions
questions.explain: A Class D holder may not drive between midnight and 5 a.m. — no exceptions.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 6 'Teen Driving Laws': 'Conditions of a Class D Provisional License'

questions.q: During the first six months with a Class D license, who may ride with the driver?
questions.explain: In the first six months only immediate family members (including anyone living in the driver's home) may ride along.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 6 'Teen Driving Laws': 'Conditions of a Class D Provisional License'

questions.q: During the second six months with a Class D license, how many non-family passengers under 21 may ride?
questions.explain: In the second six months, only one passenger under 21 who is not immediate family may ride.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 6 'Teen Driving Laws': 'Conditions of a Class D Provisional License'

questions.q: After the first year with a Class D license, how many non-family passengers under 21 may ride with the driver?
questions.explain: After the first and second six-month periods, no more than three non-family passengers under 21 may ride.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 6 'Teen Driving Laws': 'Conditions of a Class D Provisional License'

questions.q: To upgrade from Class D to Class C at 18, a driver must have no major traffic violations during the preceding:
questions.explain: Class D holders must be free of major traffic violation convictions for the 12 months before applying for Class C.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 2 'Obtaining a License, Permit or Identification Card': 'Obtaining a Class C License - Exchanging a Class D License'

questions.q: Who may ask DDS to revoke a minor's permit or license before the minor turns 18?
options: The parent, guardian or responsible adult who signed the application
questions.explain: The adult who signed the minor's application may request revocation at any time before the 18th birthday ($10 fee, notarized form).
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 6 'Teen Driving Laws': 'Revocation of Minor's License/Permit'

questions.q: The Georgia knowledge exam for a permit has two parts. How many questions does each part have?
questions.explain: The road signs test and the road rules test each have 20 questions.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 3 'Testing Information': 'Knowledge Exam'

questions.q: How many questions must you answer correctly on each part of the Georgia knowledge exam?
questions.explain: You must correctly answer 15 of 20 on the road signs test and 15 of 20 on the road rules test.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 3 'Testing Information': 'Knowledge Exam'

questions.q: In what language is the road signs part of the Georgia knowledge exam given?
questions.explain: The road signs test and the driving test are in English only; the road rules test is offered in some other languages.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 3 'Testing Information': 'Knowledge Exam'

questions.q: If you fail part of the Class C or D knowledge or road test for the first time, when can you retake it?
questions.explain: After a first failure you must wait until the next day; after a second or later failure, you must wait 7 days.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 3 'Testing Information': 'Results of Pass/Fail'

questions.q: After failing the same test a second time, how long must you wait to retake it?
questions.explain: A second or subsequent failure requires a 7-day wait before retaking the failed portion.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 3 'Testing Information': 'Results of Pass/Fail'

questions.q: What happens if someone uses a cell phone or talks to another person during the knowledge exam?
options: The exam is counted as a failure
questions.explain: Phones and talking are not allowed; any misconduct means the exam session counts as a failure.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 3 'Testing Information': 'Knowledge Exam'

questions.q: What is the minimum score needed to pass the Class C/D road test?
questions.explain: You must achieve a minimum score of 75% on the Class C or D road test.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 3 'Testing Information': 'Road Test For Class C or D'

questions.q: What is the permit test fee in Georgia, paid before each testing attempt?
questions.explain: The test/permit fee is $10, paid before every attempt and not refunded if a test is failed.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 6 'Teen Driving Laws': 'Obtaining a Class C Instructional Permit (CP)'

questions.q: What is the minimum vision required for a Georgia non-commercial license?
options: 20/60 in one eye, with a 140-degree horizontal field of vision
questions.explain: Minimum vision is 20/60 in one eye, with or without corrective lenses, and at least 140 degrees of horizontal vision.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 1 'General Licensing Information': 'Vision Requirements'

questions.q: New Georgia residents who want to drive must get a Georgia license within how many days of becoming a resident?
questions.explain: New residents have 30 days after moving to Georgia to get a Georgia license or permit if they want to drive here.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 1 'General Licensing Information': 'Requirement to obtain a Georgia Driver's License'

questions.q: How long is a standard Georgia Class C driver's license valid, and what does it cost?
questions.explain: A Class C license is issued for 8 years at a cost of $32.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 1 'General Licensing Information': 'Fees/Forms of Payment'

questions.q: If your Georgia license has been expired for more than two years, what must you do to renew it?
options: Pass vision, knowledge (signs and rules) and road tests
questions.explain: A license expired more than two years requires the vision test, the driving test, and the road signs and rules knowledge exams.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 1 'General Licensing Information': 'Expired License'

questions.q: Georgia drivers age 64 and older must pass a vision screening how often?
questions.explain: Customers age 64 and over must complete a vision screening every eight years.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 1 'General Licensing Information': 'Vision Requirements'

questions.q: A license restriction code 'B' on a Georgia license means:
questions.explain: Restriction code B means corrective lenses are required; 'A' means no restrictions.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 1 'General Licensing Information': 'License Restrictions'

questions.q: If an officer asks to see your license while you are driving, you must:
options: Show it only if you were speeding
Refuse until you speak to a lawyer
questions.explain: You must carry your license or permit while driving and display it to any law enforcement officer on request.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 1 'General Licensing Information': 'Carrying and Displaying Your License'

questions.q: When you are pulled over by police, you should:
options: Get out and walk to the police car
Signal, pull over safely, stay in the car and keep your hands visible
Keep driving to a well-lit place without signaling
questions.explain: Pull over safely, turn off the engine, stay in the vehicle unless told otherwise, and keep your hands where the officer can see them.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), 'What to Do and Expect When Pulled Over by Police'

questions.q: A 17-year-old who can show proof of military enlistment:
options: Must wait until age 18 to drive
Must hold a permit for two years
Is exempt from holding a permit for one year and one day
questions.explain: A 17-year-old with proof of military enlistment is exempt from the one-year-and-one-day permit requirement and receives a Class C license after the road test.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 6 'Teen Driving Laws': 'Obtaining a Class D Provisional License'

questions.q: After a crash, you must notify police immediately if anyone is injured or killed, or if property damage exceeds:
questions.explain: Notify the nearest law enforcement agency if anyone is injured or killed or damage is more than $500.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 11 'Crashes': 'If You Are Involved In A Crash'

questions.q: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle, you must:
options: Find the owner or leave your name, address and vehicle owner's name in a conspicuous place
Leave if the damage looks small
questions.explain: Either locate the owner or leave a note with your name, address and the name of the vehicle owner where it can be found.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 11 'Crashes': 'If You Are Involved In A Crash'

questions.q: After a minor crash on a multilane highway with no serious injuries, if the cars can be driven you should:
options: Leave them where they are until police arrive
Leave the scene without exchanging information
Move them out of the travel lanes to the shoulder or another safe place
questions.explain: Georgia law requires moving drivable vehicles off the roadway when there is no serious injury; doing so does not imply fault.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 11 'Crashes': 'Moving Vehicles Following a Crash'

questions.q: When helping an injured person at a crash scene, you should generally:
options: Not move them unless absolutely necessary, and keep them warm
Lift them up so they can walk
questions.explain: Do not move or lift a victim unless absolutely necessary; stop bleeding with pressure and keep them warm.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 11 'Crashes': 'Aiding the Injured'

questions.q: Georgia's Good Samaritan Law:
options: Protects people from civil damages when they give emergency care
questions.explain: The Good Samaritan Law holds people harmless for civil damages arising from rendering emergency care.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 11 'Crashes': 'Aiding the Injured'

questions.q: Your vehicle stalls on railroad tracks and a train may be coming. What should you do first?
options: Push the car off the tracks
Get everyone out and move away from the tracks
Stay in the car with seat belts on
Try to restart the engine repeatedly
questions.explain: Get out immediately and move away, then find the Emergency Notification System sign and call for help.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Railroad Crossings'

questions.q: When railroad crossing signals are flashing, you must stop:
options: Within 50 feet but not closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail
questions.explain: Stop no more than 50 feet and no less than 15 feet from the nearest rail when signals flash, gates are down, or a train is near.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Railroad Crossings'

questions.q: The crossing gates are down but you do not see a train. What should you do?
options: Go under the gates if they are high enough
Stay stopped until the gates rise and signals stop flashing
questions.explain: Never drive through, around or under a lowered crossing gate; wait until all tracks are clear and gates are raised.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Railroad Crossings'

questions.q: Before crossing railroad tracks, you should make sure:
options: There is room on the other side to drive completely across without stopping
questions.explain: 'If it won't fit, don't commit' — do not enter a crossing unless you can drive completely through.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 5 'Traffic Laws': 'Railroad Crossings'

questions.q: If you have a tire blowout, you should:
options: Grip the wheel firmly, ease off the gas and let the car slow before moving to the shoulder
questions.explain: Hold the wheel firmly, take your foot off the accelerator, brake lightly if needed, and don't pull over until you have slowed greatly.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Tire Blow-Out'

questions.q: If your brakes fail, which action does the manual recommend?
options: Shift to a lower gear and use the parking brake
questions.explain: For brake failure: shift to a lower gear, use the parking brake, rub a tire against a curb if needed, and look for a safe place to stop.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Other Highway Emergencies'

questions.q: If your accelerator sticks, which action is recommended?
options: Shift to neutral, concentrate on steering, and brake
Turn the key to the lock position
questions.explain: For a jammed accelerator: slap the pedal, shift to neutral, steer, brake, and turn off the ignition (not to lock).
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Other Highway Emergencies'

questions.q: After driving through deep water, you should:
options: Speed up to dry the tires
Test and dry your brakes by driving slowly while braking lightly
Turn on your hazard lights and stop
questions.explain: Wet brakes may pull or fail; dry them by driving slowly in low gear while applying the brakes lightly.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 8 'Safety Guidelines': 'Other Highway Emergencies'

questions.q: Under Georgia's Safety Responsibility Law, if you receive a suspension order after an uninsured crash claim, you may request a hearing within:
questions.explain: You are entitled to a hearing if requested within ten days of receiving the suspension order.
questions.ref: Georgia Drivers Manual (DDS online edition, 2026), Section 10 'Losing Your Driving Privileges': 'Safety Responsibility Law'
